judged_text: The updateAllCalendarEvents loop lacks the `if (credential)` guard that the parallel createAllCalendarEvents code has: after the in-memory filter and the new DB fetch fail, `credential` is undefined and is passed straight into `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` One unresolvable credential makes updateEvent throw; since the loop's promises are collected and awaited inside the surrounding try, the outer catch converts the failure into `appName: "none", success: false` results for every calendar reference — including ones whose updates actually succeeded — so the response misreports the whole reschedule as failed and hides which credential was broken

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` (the reschedule/update path), inside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop the code resolves `credential` from `this.calendarCredentials` and, if missing, attempts a DB fetch. But unlike `createAllCalendarEvents`, there is no `if (credential)` guard before calling `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))`. If both lookups fail, `credential` remains `undefined` and is passed into `updateEvent(...)`, which will likely throw/reject when it tries to use the credential. The surrounding `try/catch` then returns a failure result for every calendar reference (`calendarReference?.map(...)`), masking any successful updates and misreporting the overall outcome.
